rv.q: Lewis seems less interested in wowing us with his skills of illusion and uncanny perception than in getting us to laugh — and he does, big time. That's the real magic.
Like its sister shows, this is a goofy, but intelligent mix of silliness and sophistication.
'Mind Mangler' provides a fair amount of entertainment; and if you bring the kids, so much the better as it provides them with adult entertainment they can howl at and feel quite sophisticated.
Two hours is far too long for this sort of mechanical gaggery; some ruthless editing would improve the show markedly.
The two-hour show, directed by Hannah Sharkey, is too long for its good.
The magic of 'Mind Mangler' is in the performances, which are a perfect treat any time of year.
This may not be considered to be good theatre, but it does fall into the category of good entertainment.
Mr. Lewis masterfully worked the audience interactions, which were infinitely more entertaining than the tricks.
Even though 'Mind Mangler' doesn't really seem to have something to say, it does show that 'Life can be fun'—and maybe that's worthwhile enough.
Although some of the illusions actually worked, they are overshadowed by the planned screw-ups.
Though the audience was full of children on the afternoon I attended, the play is marginally family-friendly, and Lewis often seemed more bothered than amused at having to deal with the kids.

cn.t: Critics find this comedy-magic show amusing but overlong, with mixed reactions on its family-friendliness. Lewis's audience interaction earns laughs, though the "goes wrong" formula feels repetitive at two hours.
